source: Cabal's own adjudication cases, in the DATC JSON layout of tests/data/datc_v3.json plus explicit lists: `dislodged` (every dislodged unit and its attacker's origin), `standoffs` (every standoff province) and `retreats` (legal retreat destinations by the dislodged unit's province). Each case states a ruling that follows directly from the rulebook and that the DATC layout cannot express.

cases.name: x01_bounce_is_a_standoff_when_both_bouncing_units_are_dislodged
cases.note: Munich and Vienna bounce in Tyrolia; each is dislodged from a third province. A dislodged unit only loses its effect on the province its attacker came from, so Tyrolia is a standoff and closed to both retreats.

cases.name: x03_head_to_head_loser_leaves_no_standoff_behind_its_attacker
cases.note: The loser of a head-to-head battle has no effect on the province its attacker came from. Burgundy is closed to Munich as the attacker's origin, not as a standoff.

cases.name: x04_a_third_unit_takes_the_province_behind_a_head_to_head_winner
cases.note: Burgundy beats Munich head to head and leaves Burgundy vacant. Munich's failed move there does not stop Paris from walking in.

cases.name: x05_plain_bounce_is_a_standoff_and_closes_the_province_to_retreats
cases.note: Berlin and Warsaw bounce in Silesia while Munich is dislodged from Burgundy: Munich may go to neither Silesia (standoff) nor Burgundy (attacker's origin).
